title: Smt. Kudusia Begum v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed; no interference where the statutory appeal against the final assessment was not filed.
headnote: Where an earlier writ seeking to quash a final assessment had already been dismissed for the alternative statutory remedy of appeal, and the consumer admitted that no appeal had been filed, the High Court declined to interfere with a later Tehsildar recovery citation for the assessed electricity dues and dismissed the writ.
facts: Smt. Kudusia Begum challenged a 20 April 2022 Tehsildar recovery citation from Tehsil Karchhana, Prayagraj, claiming Rs 9,85,010 plus charges as electricity dues. She sought quashing of the citation, a fresh Electricity Supply Code 2005 assessment after hearing, decision on her 24 August 2021 representation, and a stay of coercive recovery. Her earlier writ against the 16 July 2021 final assessment had been dismissed on 23 October 2021 for the statutory appeal; she admitted no appeal had been filed.

holding_units.holding: Once an earlier writ against a final assessment has been dismissed for the alternative statutory remedy of appeal, and the consumer admits that no appeal was filed, a later writ seeking to quash a Tehsildar recovery citation for those dues, a fresh Supply Code assessment, and a stay of coercive recovery calls for no interference and is dismissed.
holding_units.flag: Order refers only to the 'alternative statutory remedy of filing an appeal' without numbering the section; s.127 inferred from an unappealed final assessment.

principle_tags.application: The Court treated the petitioner's admitted failure to file the statutory appeal against the 16.07.2021 final assessment — after an earlier writ had already been dismissed on that ground — as conclusive against a later challenge to the Tehsildar recovery citation.

lead_authorities.name: Smt. Kudusia Begum v. State of U.P., Writ-C No. 27451 of 2021 (23.10.2021)

not_decided.point: Merits of the 16.07.2021 final assessment and of the 20.04.2022 recovery citation
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine whether the assessment or the Tehsildar citation complied with the Electricity Supply Code 2005.
